extracted.intended_audience: YouTube users, creators, platform policy readers, and researchers interested in recommendation behavior
extracted.subtask_description: Official description of how YouTube's recommendation system works, including what signals and surfaces (homepage, Up Next) are used and how high-quality information and contextual labels are elevated and presented for sensitive topics like news and health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core job of recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: At the highest level, our recommendations system is designed to anticipate and meet a user's needs to drive value through relevant and satisfying viewing experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations should help people find the videos they want to watch and that will give them value; the system's purpose is delivering relevant and satisfying viewing experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of user signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding a user's viewing behavior, likes, dislikes, subscriptions, and feedback, including from satisfaction surveys, helps us do this most effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations are driven by personalized signals such as watch history, likes/dislikes, subscriptions and explicit feedback (e.g., satisfaction surveys); these signals guide what content is surfaced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of channel reputation and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: We also consider the reputation and the quality of a channel to determine how, when, and to whom the content can be surfaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel-level assessments influence ranking and visibility; external evaluators are used to help understand how an average viewer might perceive the content to ensure users have a high-quality experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: User data controls
rubrics_metrics.description: We’ve built controls that help people decide how much data they want to provide. Users can always pause, edit, or delete their YouTube search and watch history whenever they want.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can opt to limit personalization by pausing or deleting watch/search history; the system accounts for logged-out users or those who don't share data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homepage recommendations surface
rubrics_metrics.description: A user’s homepage is what you see when you first open YouTube—when a user is logged in, it displays a mixture of personalized recommendations, subscriptions, and the latest news and information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homepage is a primary surface combining personalization, subscriptions, and timely news; breaking news shelf may also appear here for major events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Up Next panel behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: This appears when you’re watching a video and suggests additional content based on what you’re currently watching, alongside other videos that we think you may be interested in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Up Next recommends videos related to the current video and other personalized interests, guiding continued viewing sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevating high-quality information for sensitive topics
rubrics_metrics.description: For topics where accuracy and high-quality are key — like news, personal finance, and medical and scientific information — we elevate high-quality voices using a variety of tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitive or high-stakes topics receive special treatment to surface authoritative or high-quality sources rather than relying solely on generic engagement signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search results prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: Search results are prioritized to provide the best search results for the user based on relevance, engagement and quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevance, engagement, and quality are all considered when ranking search results, with differing importance depending on the type of search (i.e., the balance of those three factors changes by query intent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch Next ranking signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Video suggestions appear in Watch Next, guiding users to new content based on their watch history, broader viewer trends, and current video topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch Next mixes individual watch history with aggregate viewer trends and topical signals to recommend subsequent content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News shelf policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When a major breaking news event happens, the breaking news shelf appears directly on the homepage, featuring relevant videos related to a specific breaking news topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During major events, a dedicated breaking news shelf surfaces relevant videos prominently on the homepage to help users find timely coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top News / news shelf behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: When searching for a news topic, the news shelf appears near the top of the results with relevant videos from high quality sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News-related searches surface a 'news shelf' prioritized near the top, favoring videos from high-quality sources to provide reliable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health information shelf
rubrics_metrics.description: When searching for a specific health topic, the health content shelf will highlight videos from high quality sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Health-related queries trigger a dedicated shelf that emphasizes authoritative or high-quality health content to reduce misinformation risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information panels for publisher context
rubrics_metrics.description: Information panels on the video Watch page make it easier for users to assess an organization's background (e.g., government or public funding for news publishers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual panels provide background about publishers and funding to help viewers evaluate source credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labels for altered or synthetic media
rubrics_metrics.description: We require that creators disclose realistic content that is made with altered or synthetic media, including content made with GenAI, and then labels appear on the video or in its description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators must disclose synthetic/altered realistic content (including GenAI); YouTube displays labels on the video or in descriptions to inform viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of information panels more broadly
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide additional context about certain events, topics, and publishers, we use information panel across YouTube.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information panels are a general tool to add context across content types—used for events, topics, and publisher background to help viewers assess content.
